### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you looking to use your mix of field and analytical skills to recover endangered Sierra Nevada bighorn sheep? The Department of Fish and Wildlife is seeking a motivated individual to work as an Environmental Scientist in the Sierra Bighorn Recovery Program.
  
  
The position will focus on Sierra Nevada bighorn sheep but will also include work on their predators. Data collection will include field work such as helicopter and ground surveys (hiking and backpacking). The incumbent will be responsible for wildlife management and analysis of large spatial and demographic datasets; excellent R coding is essential.

The incumbent will run Bayesian integrated population models that use estimates of abundance, vital rates, and spatial data for Sierra Nevada bighorn sheep. Participate in captures to deploy GPS collars, collect nutritional data using ultrasonography, conduct disease surveillance and genetic sampling. Use GIS and statistical methods to inform reintroduction efforts. Conduct, and analyze threats to the recovery of Sierra bighorn. Analyze large scale climate data to project and interpret its effects on Sierra bighorn recovery. Analyze environmental, habitat, and predation threats that influence progress towards recovery goals. The incumbent will also assist in maintaining consumptive and non-consumptive uses of wildlife.  
  
  

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

  

Personal Leave Program - Human Resources - CalHR.

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in-person at least four (4) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N-22-25. Additional in-office days may be required based on operational needs.

Environmental Scientist: Exam Bulletin Link

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Must be able to work in various habitats including but not limited to high altitudes (8,000 – 14,000 feet), arid environments and valley, grassland, conifer and riparian habitats, in inclement weather, and in rugged backcountry terrain during all months of the year. This position will require wildlife restraint certification to chemically immobilize animals. Travel up to 40% multiple nights for fieldwork and will attend meetings and conferences as directed. This position offers the possibility of an office-centered telework agreement based on the Department's current Telework Policy. As a condition of employment, the incumbent may be required to wear an appropriate uniform consistent with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901) for various work situations, including field surveys and public interaction, both within and outside the Region as required by the supervisor.

We draw from more than 20 technical specialties worldwide and are committed to fostering an inclusive community of diverse talents, backgrounds, and expertise. The successful candidate will function as an experienced professional who applies advanced practical knowledge, exercises independent judgment, and resolves complex technical and project-delivery issues within established professional and regulatory practices. EnSafe is seeking a full-time Environmental Scientist/Project Manager to join our team of professionals at our San Diego or Long Beach CA, office.

This position has a requirement to work onsite, at the San Diego or Long Beach, CA office, if needed relocation assistance may be offered to meet this expectation.

**What we are looking for**

An Environmental Scientist with proven experience managing environmental due diligence projects and a strong ability to translate complex findings into clear, defensible Phase I ESA reports. You'll work with clients across California and beyond, managing projects from site assessment through final reporting while gaining exposure to Phase II investigations, environmental sampling, and emerging areas such as PFAS risk evaluation.

Joining our team means immersing yourself in an environment that nurtures creativity, encourages collaboration at all levels, fosters a supportive culture, and facilitates professional development.

***Key responsibilities of this position include***

***What you will be doing:***

* Perform and manage Phase I Environmental Site Assessments in accordance with ASTM and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Conduct site reconnaissance, historical research, regulatory database review, interviews, and other due diligence activities.
* Prepare clear, technically sound Phase I ESA reports and recommendations.
* Manage multiple Phase I ESA projects, including scope, schedule, budget, subcontractors, client communication, and deliverables.
* Provide technical and peer review of Phase I ESA reports as experience permits.
* Support Phase II environmental site investigations and other due diligence activities when warranted.
* Plan and conduct environmental sampling activities involving soil, groundwater, soil vapor, indoor air, surface water, or other environmental media.
* Prepare work plans, technical memoranda, investigation reports, and proposals.
* Communicate findings and environmental risk considerations clearly to clients and project teams.
* Coordinate work with junior staff and provide technical guidance and mentoring.
* Support environmental compliance projects based on experience and workload, which may include hazardous materials and hazardous waste management, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, EPCRA/Tier II, or related regulatory requirements.
* Participate in business development activities, including preparation of scopes, budgets, proposals, and support for existing client relationships.
* Travel periodically to project sites throughout California and as needed, elsewhere in the United States.

***Minimum Skills and Requirements***

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, Geology, Environmental Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering discipline.
* Approximately 6 or more years of relevant environmental consulting experience.
* Demonstrated experience preparing Phase I Environmental Site Assessments.
* Strong technical writing and report preparation skills.
* Ability to independently conduct site reconnaissance and evaluate environmental conditions.
* Working knowledge of environmental due diligence practices and applicable federal and state environmental regulations.
* Ability to manage schedules, budgets, client expectations, and multiple concurrent assignments.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel to support project work.
* Valid driver's license and ability to perform field activities associated with environmental site assessments.

***Preferred Qualifications***

***The following experience would be beneficial but is not required:***

* Experience managing Phase I ESA programs or providing technical/peer review.
* Qualification as an Environmental Professional under ASTM/AAI requirements.
* Phase II ESA, subsurface investigation, soil, groundwater, or vapor assessment experience.
* Environmental compliance experience, including hazardous waste, hazardous materials, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, CERS/HMBP, or EPCRA/Tier II reporting.
* Experience supporting industrial, commercial real estate, logistics/warehouse, energy, municipal, or similar clients.
* Professional Geologist (PG), Professional Engineer (PE), or other relevant professional certification.
* Building sciences or hazardous building materials experience.
* Experience with asbestos-containing materials, lead-based paint, mold/microbial assessments, or related building surveys.
* California asbestos or lead certifications.
* 40-hour HAZWOPER training.

  EnSafe's mission focuses on impactful environmental, health, and safety consulting—making a real difference in communities and is backed by its long-standing technical credibility.

jobs.title: Utah Watershed Restoration & Partnerships Manager
jobs.description:
This is a remote position that must be based in Utah's Greater Salt Lake region (e.g., Salt Lake City, Ogden, Logan, Park City, Heber City, or Provo).

**About the Program**

WRI's U.S. Forests and Water program, part of the global Cities4Forests initiative, works to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire, restore degraded forests, and protect watersheds across the U.S. The program focuses on designing, implementing, financing, and scaling projects with local partners to build disaster resilience, strengthen water security, protect and enhance infrastructure, create jobs and recreation opportunities, and boost rural prosperity.

In Utah, WRI has served as a strategic partner for the U.S. Forest Service, water and electric utilities, state agencies, conservation organizations, academia, and local governments for nearly a decade and has worked to improve watershed health and reduce wildfire risk across the Great Salt Lake Basin. A key component of this work is the Utah Resilience Fund, an innovative fund that brings together public, private, and philanthropic funding to scale watershed restoration and long-term resilience. Additional information on the U.S. project portfolio can be found here.

**Job Highlight**

The Utah Watershed Restoration Manager will help advance watershed restoration, partnerships, and resilience projects across Utah, with an initial emphasis on the Jordan River watershed and its forested source watersheds. This position is focused on developing a pipeline of restoration projects from planning to implementation by coordinating partners, advancing policy priorities, supporting funding acquisition, and helping deliver on-the-ground restoration outcomes at scale.

Working closely with the Utah Watershed Resilience Manager, Research & Project Development Manager, Cities4Forests' senior leadership and a diverse network of local partners, the Manager will build and maintain relationships with municipalities, water providers, conservation districts, state and federal agencies, community organizations, and other stakeholders. The role will help identify restoration opportunities, remove implementation barriers, navigate policy and permitting processes, secure project funding, and support successful project delivery.

The successful candidate brings a strong understanding of Utah's water, watershed, forest, and wildfire landscape, an established network of relationships within the Greater Salt Lake region, and experience coordinating complex environmental or infrastructure projects. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys working directly with communities and partners to turn plans into action and create measurable benefits for watersheds, communities, and ecosystems.

**What You Will Do**

**Restoration Planning & Watershed Leadership (40%)**

  

* Lead planning, implementation, and scaling of watershed restoration and resilience projects across priority watersheds, with an initial focus on the Jordan River watershed and Greater Salt Lake Basin.
* Partner with utilities, local governments, agencies, NGOs, and land managers to identify, prioritize, and advance restoration projects that improve watershed health, water security, and wildfire resilience.
* Help utilities consider financing approaches for integrated grey and green infrastructure strategies.
* Help move projects from concept to implementation by supporting project development, permitting, funding, stakeholder coordination, and delivery across public and private lands.

**About the Program**

WRI's U.S. Forests and Water program, part of the global Cities4Forests initiative, works to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire, restore degraded forests, and protect watersheds across the U.S. The program focuses on designing, implementing, financing, and scaling projects with local partners to build disaster resilience, strengthen water security, protect and enhance infrastructure, create jobs and recreation opportunities, and boost rural prosperity.

In Utah, WRI has served as a strategic partner for the U.S. Forest Service, water and electric utilities, state agencies, conservation organizations, academia, and local governments for nearly a decade and has worked to improve watershed health and reduce wildfire risk across the Great Salt Lake Basin. A key component of this work is the Utah Resilience Fund, an innovative fund that brings together public, private, and philanthropic funding to scale watershed restoration and long-term resilience. Additional information on the U.S. project portfolio can be found here.

**Job Highlight**

The Utah Watershed Restoration Manager will help advance watershed restoration, partnerships, and resilience projects across Utah, with an initial emphasis on the Jordan River watershed and its forested source watersheds. This position is focused on developing a pipeline of restoration projects from planning to implementation by coordinating partners, advancing policy priorities, supporting funding acquisition, and helping deliver on-the-ground restoration outcomes at scale.

Working closely with the Utah Watershed Resilience Manager, Research & Project Development Manager, Cities4Forests' senior leadership and a diverse network of local partners, the Manager will build and maintain relationships with municipalities, water providers, conservation districts, state and federal agencies, community organizations, and other stakeholders. The role will help identify restoration opportunities, remove implementation barriers, navigate policy and permitting processes, secure project funding, and support successful project delivery.

The successful candidate brings a strong understanding of Utah's water, watershed, forest, and wildfire landscape, an established network of relationships within the Greater Salt Lake region, and experience coordinating complex environmental or infrastructure projects. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys working directly with communities and partners to turn plans into action and create measurable benefits for watersheds, communities, and ecosystems.

**What You Will Do**

**Restoration Planning & Watershed Leadership (40%)**

  

* Lead planning, implementation, and scaling of watershed restoration and resilience projects across priority watersheds, with an initial focus on the Jordan River watershed and Greater Salt Lake Basin.
* Partner with utilities, local governments, agencies, NGOs, and land managers to identify, prioritize, and advance restoration projects that improve watershed health, water security, and wildfire resilience.
* Help utilities consider financing approaches for integrated grey and green infrastructure strategies.
* Help move projects from concept to implementation by supporting project development, permitting, funding, stakeholder coordination, and delivery across public and private lands.
* Support development of near- and long-term restoration strategies informed by watershed science, wildfire risk, partner priorities, and implementation readiness.
* Track project performance, budgets, and outcomes, and support monitoring and evaluation efforts.

**Partnership Building & Policy Engagement (40%)**

  

* Build trusted relationships with utilities, local governments, conservation organizations, state and federal agencies, community groups, and other partners.
* Lead watershed collaboratives, technical committees, and partner working groups to align priorities and accelerate restoration outcomes.
* Monitor and participate in water, forestry, wildfire, and watershed policy discussions relevant to WRI's work and restoration goals.
* Identify opportunities to align restoration priorities with local, state, and federal programs and funding sources.
* Develop recommendations and strategies that remove barriers to implementation and increase investment in watershed resilience.

**Fundraising, Communications & Outreach (20%)**

  

* Lead the drafting of grant proposals and funding applications to support the work in Utah.
* Develop and steward opportunities and relationships with current and prospective donors.
* Represent WRI and the Utah Resilience Fund at conferences, workshops, utility meetings, and stakeholder events.

* Support efforts to position Utah as a national leader in watershed resilience and conservation finance.
* Contribute to publications, blogs, webinars, and other outreach activities that share best practices and elevate project visibility.
